decision_context: A national public-health agency convenes a medical panel to decide whether a decades-long observational study of an untreated chronic transmissible infection should continue after renewed internal objections.
decision_question: Should the programme continue substantially as designed, be modified, or terminate now?
available_actions: Continue observation without routinely offering the established curative treatment to the infected study group.
Modify the study while preserving some longitudinal follow-up.
End the untreated-study design, disclose relevant facts and offer established treatment.
Suspend continuation pending independent ethical and scientific review.

affected_parties.party: Several hundred adult participants from a historically marginalised population, including an infected study group
affected_parties.known_interests_or_risks: Health, life, bodily autonomy, truthful information, access to effective treatment and freedom from research exploitation.
Risk from an untreated transmissible infection and family consequences of serious illness.
Scientific value of long-term observations, institutional reputation and continuity of a long-running programme.
Potential benefit of scientific knowledge and confidence that research institutions will not exploit participants.

known_evidence.claim: The programme began decades earlier to observe the natural history of the infection and includes an infected group and a control group.
Participants were not given informed consent to an untreated-disease experiment and were led to believe they were receiving health care for a broad illness description.
A highly effective treatment has been the accepted treatment of choice and widely available for many years, but participants have not routinely been offered it by the study.
An internal adviser has raised ethical objections and asked leadership to reconsider continuation.
Supporters of continuation argue that the long longitudinal dataset is scientifically unique and cannot be recreated if treatment changes the course of disease.
The untreated infection can cause severe illness, death and transmission; the incremental scientific value of further untreated observation is uncertain.

known_uncertainties: How much additional useful information further untreated observation would produce.
How much scientific value can be preserved through consensual follow-up after treatment.
What remediation is feasible for harms already incurred.
known_alternatives: End the untreated component and offer treatment while continuing consensual follow-up.
Use existing data without imposing further untreated exposure.
Submit any proposed continuation to independent ethics oversight.
Seek genuinely informed consent for any remaining non-therapeutic research that is independently judged permissible.
requested_output: Identify affected parties and power asymmetries.
Assess each available action under the Moral Code using only this packet.
Identify any moral-floor or protected-freedom breach.
Identify the least harmful feasible alternative.
State uncertainty and evidence that could change the judgement.
